title: CallLint identity conflict
description: An UNRESOLVED identity collision, recorded as a first-class row rather than handled as an exception (calllint.identity-conflict.v1; §7.1, §10.2, ADR 0061). This schema exists because the fail-closed path needs somewhere to put its output: when two source records claim one identity, the compiler must refuse to merge them, and a refusal that is only a thrown error loses the very evidence a human needs to adjudicate it. So `sourceRecordIds` carries every record that participated in the collision — a conflict naming one record is not a conflict, which is why `minItems` is 2. `status` never silently drains: `OPEN` and `ACKNOWLEDGED` both keep the affected subject at identityStatus CONFLICT (terminal, per calllint.canonical-subject.v1), and only an explicit `RESOLVED` with a `resolution` object may release it. `resolvedAt` and `resolution` are nullable in lockstep with that: a resolved conflict without a recorded resolution would be indistinguishable from a dropped one. Written by R-3; the table and schema land in R-1 with the rest of the canonical DDL.
